class.name: NoiseGenerator
class.brief_description: Noise generator for terrain height and density sampling using Godot's Noise system.
class.description:
[b]NoiseGenerator[/b] is a wrapper around Godot's [Noise] class that provides convenient configuration for terrain generation. It handles both 2D (height) and 3D (density) noise sampling with customizable parameters.
[b]Key Features:[/b] [ul] [li]2D noise for base terrain height sampling[/li] [li]3D noise for detailed terrain density/caves[/li] [li]Configurable octaves, persistence, lacunarity, and period[/li] [li]Seed-based deterministic generation[/li] [li]Serializable to .tres for reusable presets[/li] [/ul]
[b]Typical Usage:[/b] [code] # Create and configure for base terrain var terrain_noise = NoiseGenerator.new() terrain_noise.set_period(64.0) # Feature wavelength terrain_noise.set_octaves(6) # Detail layers terrain_noise.set_persistence(0.5) # Amplitude decay per octave terrain_noise.set_lacunarity(2.0) # Frequency multiplier per octave terrain_noise.set_seed(42)
generator.set_terrain_noise(terrain_noise)
# Create for detail/rocky features var detail_noise = NoiseGenerator.new() detail_noise.set_period(16.0) detail_noise.set_octaves(4) generator.set_detail_noise(detail_noise) [/code]
[b]Noise Parameters Explained:[/b] [ul] [li][b]seed:[/b] Random seed. Same seed = same noise pattern. Change for different terrain.[/li] [li][b]period:[/b] Wavelength of noise features (in voxels). Larger = bigger mountains/features.[/li] [li][b]octaves:[/b] Number of noise layers combined. More = more detail but slower.[/li] [li][b]persistence:[/b] How much each octave contributes. 0.0-1.0. Higher = rougher terrain.[/li] [li][b]lacunarity:[/b] Frequency multiplier per octave. Typical: 2.0. Controls fine detail scale.[/li] [/ul]
[b]Related Classes:[/b] [ul] [li][VoxelGenerator] - Uses this for terrain height and detail[/li] [li][TerrainConfig] - Can reference a NoiseGenerator preset[/li] [li][Noise] - Godot's built-in noise class (wrapped by this)[/li] [/ul]

method.name: get_noise_3d
method.description:
Samples 3D noise at world coordinates.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]x, y, z[/code] - World position to sample.
[b]Return Value:[/b] Noise value (typically -1.0 to 1.0).
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call from any thread.
[b]Use Case:[/b] Used for density fields and detailed terrain features.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var noise_val = terrain_noise.get_noise_3d(100.0, 20.0, 150.0) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_noise_2d]

method.name: get_noise_2d
method.description:
Samples 2D noise at horizontal coordinates (ignores Y).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]x, z[/code] - Horizontal world position.
[b]Return Value:[/b] Noise value (typically -1.0 to 1.0).
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call from any thread.
[b]Use Case:[/b] Used for heightmap generation and terrain base height.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var height = terrain_noise.get_noise_2d(100.0, 150.0) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_noise_3d]

method.name: set_seed
method.description:
Sets the random seed for reproducible noise.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_seed[/code] - Seed integer (default varies). Same seed produces identical noise pattern.
[b]Effect:[/b] Seeds the internal Godot Noise object. Change this to get different terrain with same octaves/period.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var noise1 = NoiseGenerator.new() noise1.set_seed(42) noise1.set_period(64.0)
var noise2 = NoiseGenerator.new() noise2.set_seed(43) # Different seed, different pattern noise2.set_period(64.0) # But same scale [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_seed]

method.name: get_seed
method.description:
Returns the current seed.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_seed]

method.name: set_noise
method.description:
Sets the underlying Godot [Noise] object.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_noise[/code] - A Godot Noise resource (FastNoiseLite, etc.).
[b]Effect:[/b] Allows using custom Noise implementations. Advanced usage.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var custom_noise = FastNoiseLite.new() custom_noise.set_noise_type(FastNoiseLite.TYPE_PERLIN) generator.set_noise(custom_noise) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_noise]

method.name: get_noise
method.description:
Returns the underlying Godot Noise object.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_noise]

method.name: set_octaves
method.description:
Sets the number of noise octaves (detail layers).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_octaves[/code] - Number of layers. Default varies. Typical range: 1-8.
[b]Effect:[/b] Each octave adds finer detail. More octaves = more detailed terrain but slower generation. [ul] [li]1 octave: Smooth, simple terrain[/li] [li]4 octaves: Good balance of detail and speed[/li] [li]8+ octaves: Very detailed but slow[/li] [/ul]
[b]Example:[/b] [code] # For large-scale mountains terrain_noise.set_octaves(8)
# For smaller, faster terrain detail_noise.set_octaves(3) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_octaves], [method set_persistence]

method.name: get_octaves
method.description:
Returns the current number of octaves.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_octaves]

method.name: set_period
method.description:
Sets the period (wavelength) of the base noise frequency.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_period[/code] - Period in world units. Default varies. Typical: 16.0-256.0.
[b]Effect:[/b] Controls the scale of terrain features: [ul] [li]Small period (16.0): Detailed, rough terrain[/li] [li]Medium period (64.0): Balanced mountains and valleys[/li] [li]Large period (200.0): Vast, gentle rolling hills[/li] [/ul]
[b]Example:[/b] [code] # Large mountains terrain_noise.set_period(100.0)
# Fine detail detail_noise.set_period(16.0) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_period], [method set_lacunarity]

method.name: get_period
method.description:
Returns the current period.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_period]

method.name: set_persistence
method.description:
Sets the persistence factor (amplitude decay per octave).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_persistence[/code] - Factor 0.0-1.0. Default varies.
[b]Effect:[/b] Controls how much each octave contributes: [ul] [li]Low (0.2): Fine detail fades quickly, smooth terrain[/li] [li]Medium (0.5): Balanced detail contribution[/li] [li]High (0.8): Fine detail dominates, very rough terrain[/li] [/ul]
[b]Example:[/b] [code] # Smooth terrain terrain_noise.set_persistence(0.3)
# Very rocky detail detail_noise.set_persistence(0.7) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_persistence], [method set_octaves]

method.name: get_persistence
method.description:
Returns the current persistence.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_persistence]

method.name: set_lacunarity
method.description:
Sets the lacunarity (frequency multiplier per octave).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_lacunarity[/code] - Multiplier. Default 2.0. Typical: 1.5-3.0.
[b]Effect:[/b] Controls how quickly frequency increases between octaves: [ul] [li]Low (1.5): Gradual frequency increase, smoother transition[/li] [li]Standard (2.0): Each octave twice the frequency[/li] [li]High (3.0): Rapid frequency increase, varied detail scales[/li] [/ul]
[b]Example:[/b] [code] terrain_noise.set_lacunarity(2.0) # Standard [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_lacunarity], [method set_period]

method.name: get_lacunarity
method.description:
Returns the current lacunarity.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_lacunarity]
